note: MCInst_Init marks every MCOperand slot kInvalid but never initializes the RegVal/ImmVal/FPImmVal union, so for a TBEGIN MCInst that later receives only one operand, Operands[1].ImmVal remains uninitialized.
The TBEGIN decode (case 71) creates exactly one MCOperand (the 1-bit immediate from Inst{21}), so MI->size becomes 1 and Operands[1] is never written.
MCInst_getOperand performs no bounds check, so requesting operand index 1 of the 1-operand TBEGIN MCInst returns the untouched Operands[1] slot.

The asm-writer table (case 18) prints TBEGIN operand 1 as a u1imm even though the decoder produced only one operand (index 0) and the MCInstrDesc declares operand 1 as MCOI_OPERAND_UNKNOWN; this operand-layout disagreement causes the printer to read the never-initialized operand.
MCOperand_getImm returns the uninitialized ImmVal of the kInvalid operand 1, so Value carries the uninitialized bytes.
The uninitialized Value is consumed to emit the TBEGIN operand text (and mirrored into detail->ppc.operands[].imm), i.e. an uninitialized value is used when printing the PowerPC TBEGIN instruction.
